messages:
Clara (People Ops): Quick thread for end-of-cycle escalation routing + 'review clock' questions. Two small changes: an explicit emergency-extension path and a reviewer-coverage credit note. TL;DR below.

Dmitri (Eng Manager): What's the emergency-extension path?

Clara (People Ops): If something genuinely blocks completion (LOA, severe import failure, infra outage), use the Emergency Extension form: https://rwd.in/emergency-extension. That auto-creates a ticket and pauses the review clock for affected packets. We will aim to respond within 6 business hours for weekday ops.

Yvonne (Reviewer): What does "pause the review clock" mean? I've been manually tracking deadlines.

Clara (People Ops): The review clock is the internal timer we use for handback SLAs. When paused, automated reminders stop and the packet is excluded from SLA reports until the extension is approved. This avoids penalizing teams for platform issues or approved LOAs.

ClockBot: Reminder: Review clock state is visible in the Console > Review Ops > Packet status. States: running, paused, extended, closed.

Ibrahim (IC): If my reviewer picked up extra packets because someone went on leave, how do they get credit?

Clara (People Ops): Two ways to credit: 1) Mark overtime on the Emergency Extension form when requesting coverage, or 2) submit reviewer-credit form after close: https://rwd.in/reviewer-credit with PR links / packet ids. Credit shows up on the reviewer activity roster and factors into the quarterly reviewer appreciation program.

Dmitri (Eng Manager): For cross-band swaps we had confusion last time about manager approvals. Any change?

Clara (People Ops): Slight tweak: auto-swap allowed if replacement reviewer is same band OR a senior peer in the same geographic region. Otherwise manager approval required. The swap form now asks for "auto-approve" checkbox and will validate band via HR data. If auto-approve fails, people-ops is notified for manual routing.

Yvonne (Reviewer): Filing: what fields are mandatory on the swap/emergency forms?

Clara (People Ops): Mandatory fields: packet id, original reviewer, proposed reviewer (if swap), reason, expected duration of swap/extension, manager sign-off (email or slack mention) for cross-band. Attach logs for tooling errors if applicable.

Ibrahim (IC): Does a paused clock impact calibration schedules?

Clara (People Ops): Paused packets are removed from the upcoming tranche import. They will be included in the next available tranche once unpaused. If a paused packet holds a calibration anchor, people-ops will notify stewards and either move the anchor to a later tranche or use a substitute anchor. We try to avoid surprise changes to calibration agendas.

Dmitri (Eng Manager): Are there limits to extensions? People kept asking for multi-week windows last cycle.

Clara (People Ops): Standard emergency extension caps at 14 calendar days. For longer accommodations (medical parental leave, long-term disability), we use the LOA process in Workday which will create a manual reassign + potential review timeline adjustments. Anything beyond 14 days requires HR case.

ClockBot: Note: Emergency Extension requests filed after 16:00 PT may be processed next business day if they require manual steward intervention.

Yvonne (Reviewer): One small ops ask: can we get an export of paused packets per manager? Makes follow-up easier.

Clara (People Ops): Good idea. Will add a "paused packets by manager" CSV to the console exports by EOD tomorrow.

Ibrahim (IC): If a packet is paused and later unpaused with minor edits, do we re-run automated plagiarism scans / tooling checks?

Clara (People Ops): Yes, unpausing triggers a quick validation pass (anonymization, file naming, minimal length). If validation fails, packet returns to owner with a single-line failure reason. This prevents broken packets from entering calibration.

Dmitri (Eng Manager): Last Q: what's the fastest way to escalate if the console shows an import error during handback close?

Clara (People Ops): Paste the import log into the Emergency Extension form and tag @people-ops in Slack. Use subject "IMPORT-URGENT" and include packet ids. We prioritise IMPORT-URGENT tickets for triage and will usually respond within 4 business hours on weekdays.

ClockBot: Final: handback window closes Mon 17:00 PT. Automated reminders: 72h, 24h, 6h.

Yvonne (Reviewer): Thanks all 44d Filed an emergency-extension in a test case to confirm flow.

Clara (People Ops): Thanks Yvonne 64f If others want a short walkthrough of the extension UI, I'll host a 20m drop-in tomorrow at 11:00 PT.
